findings.title: Feature receipt snapshot identity is discarded before audit coverage evaluation

evidence.detail: Each feature input must carry snapshot_id.
Mapping drops the nested snapshot_id and schema_version; the FeatureCompletenessRecord retains no identity.
Feature acceptance checks verified/status/file membership, without nested snapshot equality.
nestedFeatureSnapshot: foreign-feature-snapshot passes input schema and returns complete:true with current structural receipts.

findings.trigger: Pass feature evidence from a different snapshot alongside structurally current receipts for matching paths.
findings.consequence: The coverage result advertises exact snapshot binding while accepting feature evidence with another identity.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate every nested feature snapshot against the pinned inventory before normalization; retain identity in the typed feature record and report mismatches explicitly.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Public wrapper with matching nested identities remains successful; foreign/missing identities fail with a specific feature-identity diagnostic, including camelCase compatibility inputs.
findings.inference: The probe demonstrates receipt acceptance, not the quality or frequency of an actual model's feature audit.

findings.title: Cached audit inventories bypass stale-source refusal and mix source generations

evidence.detail: Feature inspection reuses a same-root inventory cache entry; stale checking is only performed on cache misses.
Coverage evaluation uses the same cache-only stale check.
Feature search reads current mutable source bytes against the cached file roster.
cachedSourceDrift: changing small inventoried source changes a fresh inventory hash but cached evaluation still returns complete:true under the old hash.

findings.trigger: Inventory a workspace, modify an inventoried implementation below the byte cap, then inspect/evaluate using the original cached snapshot id.
findings.consequence: Current source can be reported under an older snapshot, and a stale coverage result is accepted without the documented refusal.
findings.suggestedFix: Either pin immutable source bytes and read those throughout the audit, or re-attest full non-live contents before feature inspection and synthesis. Preserve live-state exclusions and project-root binding.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Cache the inventory, change a small source file, and require explicit stale refusal; writing only excluded finding/journal artifacts remains accepted. Repeat across a different cwd with identical bytes.
findings.distinctFrom: The probe modifies a small file below every cap; it does not repeat the root's native large-tail/source-exclusion probes.

findings.title: Reviewer gate accepts foreign source fingerprints and records credit under the expected identity

evidence.detail: Wrong-but-well-formed v3 fingerprints are accepted whenever declared file coverage is complete.
The production caller emits fingerprint drift as telemetry and continues gate processing.
Successful receipt gateId uses the parent's expected fingerprint; per-file hashes are sampled at credit time.
Existing regression explicitly requires accepting a wrong-but-well-formed fingerprint.
Public contract says the runtime verifies the fingerprint against the pending working-tree snapshot.
reviewerForeignFingerprint has no attestation issues/blockers and yields LOOKS_GOOD while telemetry records the foreign token.

findings.trigger: A reviewer returns LOOKS_GOOD over the same declared pending paths but with a source fingerprint different from the parent's expected token.
findings.consequence: Syntax and file membership do not establish inspected bytes; a stale assessment may be credited under an expected/current source identity and later reused as reviewed truth.
findings.suggestedFix: Bind review credit to observed file/read basis references or an immutable reviewed snapshot; reject source-content drift. Exclude unrelated metadata from the identity rather than tolerating arbitrary foreign content fingerprints. Preserve reduced-cost reuse only for unchanged reviewed bytes.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Review source generation A, change the same paths to B, submit A's receipt, and require a fresh review with no B credit. An unrelated findings/journal update with unchanged source must not cause review churn.
findings.assurance: local gate-helper probe plus static production credit trace
findings.inference: No live model or full generator finalization was run. The helper accepts foreign tokens and the caller records credit; the rate of obsolete model assessments is unmeasured.

findings.title: Ordinary reviewer receipts can omit all assessment dimensions and implementation requirements

evidence.detail: All five nested dimensions are optional; requirementCoverage is optional at the top level.
Finalization checks only reported incomplete requirements and reported block-prefixed dimensions.
The lightweight tier deliberately excludes contract-bearing changes.
Runtime semantic guard checks only that the verdict is a known label.
Normal receipt acceptance validates the declared schema, which permits omissions.
reviewerOmittedAssessment: contract file is not lightweight-eligible; dimensions:{} and no requirements have no missing top-level schema fields, no runtime verdict issue, no blockers, and LOOKS_GOOD.

findings.trigger: A normal review of a contract-bearing behavioral change returns a matching fingerprint/file roster and LOOKS_GOOD but dimensions:{} and no requirementCoverage.
findings.consequence: The harness cannot distinguish an omitted assessment from a complete clean review; a full-review policy is weakened without explicit lightweight eligibility.
findings.suggestedFix: Use typed dimension outcomes and require every ordinary-review dimension plus coverage of an established user/plan requirement roster. Permit explicit n/a with evidence and preserve the opt-in lightweight escalation mechanism.
findings.acceptanceProbe: A standard contract-file review missing a dimension or known implementation requirement is rejected or remains incomplete; a complete clean review and an explicitly eligible reduced review succeed.
findings.assurance: schema inspection, runtime verdict guard, exported gate-helper probe
findings.inference: The source/probe establish an accepted omission shape; they do not measure whether a configured reviewer model commonly emits it.

findings.title: Omitted automatic hook setting enables manifest inference despite documented trust opt-in

evidence.detail: autoFileChangeHooks is described as disabled by default and requiring explicit true for trusted projects.
The empty/default configuration leaves autoFileChangeHooks undefined; merging preserves omission.
Only value===false suppresses inference; undefined enters manifest inference.
Rust manifests produce cargo clippy and cargo test commands for changed .rs files.
Real SDK dispatch passes no normalized autoFileChangeHooks choice or explicit hook list.
Public docs promise trusted projects must explicitly set autoFileChangeHooks:true.
Hooks actually default to a bounded 300-second timeout; schema/public no-timeout prose is stale.

findings.trigger: A workspace with Cargo.toml and changed Rust files runs the normal hook gate while autoFileChangeHooks is omitted.
findings.consequence: Manifest-inferred compilers/tests can execute repository-controlled build scripts/test code without the documented trust opt-in. Users also receive conflicting timeout expectations.
findings.suggestedFix: Require config.autoFileChangeHooks===true before inference; use configured hooks otherwise. Inject the effective configuration at the SDK boundary so scope/env choices are explicit. Reconcile documentation and config timeout comments with the selected current timeout contract.
findings.acceptanceProbe: With a harmless captured runner and isolated public config fixture, omitted/false settings run no inferred commands; explicit true selects inferred commands, and explicitly configured hooks still run. Assert the actual default/override timeout sent to the executor.
findings.inference: No untrusted target-project command was executed. Cargo build-script execution is the consequence of the discovered command choice; concrete implicit selection is established statically.
findings.secondaryContractDrift: docs/agents-and-tools.md:113 and provider-config.ts:507 claim unbounded/omitted timeout, while executor forwards hook.timeoutSeconds ?? 300 at file-change-hooks.ts:1605.

findings.title: Targeted validation accepts equal-length untracked tail mutation outside the snapshot byte prefix

evidence.detail: Each changed file contributes at most 1MiB to identity.
Full size plus capped prefix are hashed; equal-length tail changes contribute identical bytes.
The tracked git diff does not contain untracked file contents.
Pre/post source refusal depends on equality of this capped snapshot id.

equalLengthUntrackedTail changes the exported value in a 1,200,028-byte untracked.ts but leaves snapshot unchanged and bundleTruncated:false; midValidationTailMutation returns status:passed and assurance:full after a further tail edit.

findings.trigger: Change a same-length source tail beyond 1MiB in an untracked file, including during targeted validation.
findings.consequence: Distinct source generations alias to one identity, so validation evidence can claim full assurance for bytes that changed mid-run.
findings.suggestedFix: Hash full file contents with incremental bounded I/O, or mark identity incomplete and refuse full/source-bound attestation. Output retention may remain capped independently. Ensure untracked source and capped diff/status tails cannot alias through length-only terms.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Real public bundle changes identity for an equal-length untracked tail edit; the real targeted-validation function rejects the same mid-hook mutation while an unchanged-source successful hook passes. Include large tracked diffs and bounded-memory controls.
findings.assurance: real local Git/SDK integration with injected harmless validation hook
findings.distinctFrom: This is the review/targeted-validation identity path with a 1MiB cap, not the root's native audit inventory 256KB snapshot probe.
findings.inference: No target-project suite or live model review ran; the probe isolates the source identity acceptance guarantee.

findings.title: Review bundles silently drop corrupt unresolved findings after quarantine

evidence.detail: list() returns only records from listWithDiagnostics and discards diagnostics.
Corrupt records are moved into .corrupt with detailed diagnostics.
The real findings consumer uses list(), making corrupted/inaccessible evidence look like an empty list.
The CLI displays finding records only when the returned list is nonempty; no lost-record state is available.
Existing corruption test covers store diagnostics, not bundle propagation.
corruptFindingConsumption: in-scope open finding disappears as findings:[], no error/diagnostic, with its file quarantined.

findings.trigger: A persisted in-scope open finding becomes malformed before get_change_review_bundle reads it.
findings.consequence: Evidence loss is presented as successful empty findings; subsequent reads may be even less diagnostic after quarantine removed the original file.
findings.suggestedFix: Return corruption/availability diagnostics through the review bundle for all evidence kinds and persist a degraded-evidence marker so later calls do not erase the loss state. Distinguish no records, stale/out-of-scope records, and unavailable records.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Seed a current unresolved finding, corrupt it, and require visible degraded/unavailable evidence plus the corruption location on the first and later bundle reads; healthy unrelated records remain available.
findings.inference: The consumer bug does not prove that every default run currently produces LocalHarnessStore finding records; that producer path is itself not established in this slice.

findings.title: Audit completion conflates inspected coverage with feature readiness and cannot certify assessed absence

evidence.detail: Every feature must be verified complete with every implementation category nonempty.
Out-of-scope exclusions apply to structural subsystem coverage, not feature readiness.
The orchestrator must not synthesize until this combined coverage/readiness result is complete.
Canonical flow promotes evidence_kind after exact reads and blocks synthesis on incomplete features.

coverageReadinessSeparation: all inventoried file/domain declarations are valid, known absence is recorded, but complete:false and missing implementation categories remain despite the feature exclusion reason.

findings.trigger: A comprehensive body audit correctly concludes that a requested capability is absent or unwired.
findings.consequence: The audit cannot graduate its inspection while reporting missing product capabilities; it is incentivized to omit a gap or over-promote readiness to satisfy the procedure.
findings.suggestedFix: Separate audit coverage from capability maturity and assurance. Support verified negative evidence and explicit feature dispositions without claiming usability. Keep unknown/uninspected states incomplete.
findings.acceptanceProbe: A source-backed assessed-absent or unwired feature can have coverageComplete:true while readinessComplete:false; an uninspected feature remains coverage-incomplete, and the root's intentionally unimplemented fixture never becomes usable.
findings.assurance: public audit-wrapper probe plus static procedure trace
findings.relationship: Counterpart to the root's existing false-positive completeness probe; consolidate at synthesis if desired, without losing the assessed-absence acceptance requirement.

domainAssessment.security: Static current trust mismatch: omitted autoFileChangeHooks selects inferred project commands despite explicit opt-in. Artifact paths/identifiers/coverage hygiene and read-only reviewer grants are useful strengths. No source credentials/private values, network, malicious command or OS-boundary test was performed; pair09/pair10 own effect/loader enforcement.
domainAssessment.correctness: Concrete public probes show foreign nested feature identity, cached generation mixing, large untracked tail aliasing and false full validation assurance; reviewer guard probes show foreign/omitted assessment acceptance. Assessed absence is blocked by readiness/coverage conflation.
domainAssessment.state-mutation: Source caches retain old identities; receipt persistence samples credit-time bytes; store quarantine hides lost evidence at the consumer. CAS/private modes/exclusive audit creation are valuable infrastructure. Generic lock/lease/recovery defects remain other-shard responsibilities.
domainAssessment.error-handling: Corruption diagnostics are dropped by the review-bundle list consumer; stale refusal is bypassed on cache hits. Current writer returns declared invalid/unconfirmed/collision errors; targeted checks distinguish skipped and post-identity failure, subject to repaired exact source identity.
domainAssessment.performance: Bounded async manifest probes, fixed cache retention, windowed per-file hashing and capped presentation output are useful. Prefix-only identities sacrifice correctness; use incremental full hashing independently from output retention. Native audit walk/hash is synchronous and not signal-driven; no latency or asymptotic workload measurement was invented.
domainAssessment.dependency-hygiene: Root manifest pins Bun1.3.5 and shared schema/type generation avoids descriptor drift. Inspection covers generation/public catalog/package contract, not a vulnerability/provenance/license audit or release execution; pair11 owns those gates. No package install or dependency mutation occurred.
domainAssessment.test-coverage: Inspected tests cover schema/grant/receipt/collision/store invariants and explicitly preserve wrong-fingerprint/native-cap behavior; injected graph/manually seeded record tests cannot prove default runtime wiring. Existing negative acceptance holes are demonstrated by two local recorded probes. No broad test-suite or live model acceptance claim is made.
domainAssessment.api-contract: Nested feature snapshots are required but ignored, ordinary assessment completeness is optional, identity caps permit false source assurance, and public hook/fingerprint/workspace claims drift. Compatibility aliases/quarantine and exact collision markers are useful preserved contracts.

coverageLimits: Exactly this shard's assigned slice is assessed; its receipt is not a guarantee of every line, every subsystem's whole content, or a body-wide installed/live acceptance result.
Only current INVENTORY.json paths are included in structuralReceipt. Root's omitted cli/release source is supplemental context-only; no excluded active release path is credited to this receipt.

Root's existing completeness and native snapshot probes were reused without rerunning. The new large-tail probe targets review/targeted-validation identity rather than native audit identity.
No source fixes, credentials/private configuration/log reads, model/network calls, package installs, external messages, or live CLI/native/foreign-toolchain tests occurred.

Pair05 owns workflow injection mismatch, leases/snapshot/main continuation; pair11 owns CI/evaluation/package gates; pair10 owns schema transformation/loader/MCP semantics. Other body-axis assessments here are explicitly parent context.

Reviewer gate probes demonstrate accepted shapes and static credit wiring, not a live model's probability of emitting stale/omitted evidence. Hook trust mismatch is a static production trace, not executed malicious code.
Historical plan declarations and latest decisions are contextual constraints; they do not prove present defects or present capability maturity.

Current design source-supported/fixture/compiled PTY counts are documentation claims with explicit remaining limits; this shard did not independently recertify the original captures or a human/screen-reader baseline.

recommendedPlanWork.problem: Audit and review/validation source identities over-credit stale or incomplete bytes.
recommendedPlanWork.scope: Full-content bounded hashing and immutable/re-attested audit snapshots; nested feature identity validation.
recommendedPlanWork.languageDecision: Repair TS producers/consumers now; no port is required.
recommendedPlanWork.acceptance: 12-source-binding-probe and 12-review-bundle-probe must reject foreign nested/cached/large-tail source generations while unchanged-source/live-state controls remain successful.
recommendedPlanWork.completionEvidence: Versioned source-basis receipts plus positive/adversarial probe JSON tied to exact source.
recommendedPlanWork.stopDeferRule: Do not add new readiness/client gates until identity can represent exact or explicitly incomplete source.

recommendedPlanWork.problem: Reviewer declarations can omit assessments or carry foreign source tokens while granting credit.
recommendedPlanWork.scope: Typed complete normal-review outcomes, requirement roster coverage, observed read/source basis and credit identity; preserve explicit lightweight escalation.
recommendedPlanWork.languageDecision: TS canonical producer/consumer contract; preserve D53 host statechart migration as a later behavior-preserving integration.
recommendedPlanWork.acceptance: Old review over changed same paths is refused; normal contract-file omitted dimensions/requirements are incomplete; unchanged-byte and eligible lightweight controls pass.
recommendedPlanWork.completionEvidence: Real set_output→host credit test and stale review integration receipt; helper tests alone are insufficient.
recommendedPlanWork.stopDeferRule: Do not widen reuse or receipt shortcuts without an unchanged-source proof.

recommendedPlanWork.problem: Coverage categories and readiness are one green gate, preventing honest assessed absence and enabling false promotion.
recommendedPlanWork.scope: Separate inspection coverage, usable/partial/unwired/absent/unknown maturity, and static/unit/integration/live assurance; require executable/negative evidence with source identities.
recommendedPlanWork.languageDecision: TS schema/service/doc update; retain open capability registry/tiering decisions D29/D33.
recommendedPlanWork.acceptance: Assessed absence can finish audit coverage without becoming ready; root's unimplemented fixture never becomes usable; uninspected feature remains incomplete.
recommendedPlanWork.completionEvidence: Coverage and readiness matrices derived from validated receipts, not plan checkmarks.
recommendedPlanWork.stopDeferRule: Retire any completion claim based solely on six populated file lists.

recommendedPlanWork.problem: Automatic inferred commands run under omitted trust configuration and timeout prose disagrees with executor.
recommendedPlanWork.scope: Effective config injection, explicit-true inference, configured-hook preservation, consistent timeout descriptions and harmless executor capture.
recommendedPlanWork.languageDecision: TS enforcement at the caller/runner boundary; native isolation does not fix this configuration semantic mismatch.
recommendedPlanWork.acceptance: Omitted/false never infer; true explicitly enables; configured hooks retain behavior; actual timeout forwarding matches the selected public contract.
recommendedPlanWork.completionEvidence: Isolated public config fixture→SDK runner acceptance with exact selected commands and timeouts.
recommendedPlanWork.stopDeferRule: Do not activate optional validation or native tools through a blanket feature-switch change.

recommendedPlanWork.problem: Evidence-store readers lack default producers and discard corruption diagnostics.
recommendedPlanWork.scope: Wire confirmed ownership/validation/review-finding records or label optional/unwired availability; propagate and retain degradation diagnostics.
recommendedPlanWork.languageDecision: TS producer/consumer integration first; native D50/D51 ownership/store architecture remains conditional measured follow-on.
recommendedPlanWork.acceptance: Actual SDK edit/check/review outcomes appear in a source-bound bundle; corrupted record remains visibly unavailable across later reads; no effect from a failed action is recorded as committed.
recommendedPlanWork.completionEvidence: Real outcome→store→bundle→CLI evidence trace, including failure and interruption paths.
recommendedPlanWork.stopDeferRule: Do not describe a record kind/exported helper as a default body capability without its producer and consuming user path.

recommendedPlanWork.scope: Expose granted/installed/healthy/semantic tiers and wire graph test impact through a real indexer accessor; separate discovered commands from executed validation.
recommendedPlanWork.languageDecision: Consume mature ecosystem tools through versioned requests/results; new authored language only with dated measurable capability rationale.
recommendedPlanWork.acceptance: One multi-package/multi-language contract task discovers consumers and tests, updates the shared interface, and validates each component with immutable diagnostic/artifact references.
recommendedPlanWork.completionEvidence: Installed/native vertical task receipt, with unsupported operations explicitly reported.
recommendedPlanWork.stopDeferRule: Keep graph/coverage/native fields partial or unknown until the default caller executes them.

recommendedPlanWork.acceptance: Failure-preserving fixed held-out workload demonstrates a promoted change actually reaches a later task and improves the declared target without added false completion.
